claims.text: An ML-accelerated thermodynamic-integration scheme can compute both solid and liquid free energies of multicomponent high-entropy alloys at a fraction of the cost of explicit ab initio molecular dynamics or TOR-TILD.
The proposed scheme can retain accuracy comparable to explicit ab initio methods for vibrational and electron–vibration contributions near fusion temperatures.
The target materials are equilibrium, partially disordered solid-solution HEAs containing as many as five or six principal elements.

Parallelized nested sampling or a similar advanced sampler will be combined with an ML potential periodically refined using a minimal set of ab initio calculations from both solid and liquid configurations.
Using a preselected small set of first-principles configurations can improve HEA screening efficiency while retaining comparable accuracy.
Refractory-based HEAs may require calculations extending to approximately 2500–3000 K to span their melting range.
Targeted ab initio reference data can parameterize accurate interatomic forces for both solid and liquid HEA configurations.
Restricting ab initio calculations to representative snapshots will reduce the number of expensive on-the-fly ab initio molecular-dynamics steps.
A progressively refined ML interatomic model can capture finite-temperature phonon-induced vibrational entropy.
The proposed ML interatomic model can capture electron–vibration interactions.
The method will provide a 10–100-fold throughput gain relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The method will provide approximately a twofold throughput improvement over TOR-TILD.
Predicted free energies and fusion properties will deviate by less than 5–10% from benchmark ab initio calculations and available experiments.
Extending explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics or TOR-TILD workflows from elemental and binary systems to multicomponent alloys entails substantially greater computational cost.
Multicomponent alloy phase spaces are largely unexplored and impractical to map exhaustively by experiment.
Strong short-range order or phase separation may invalidate assumptions underlying the proposed ML potential.
The method is valid only when its ab initio reference set sufficiently samples the relevant atomic arrangements.
Pronounced local distortions or magnetic ordering can reduce accuracy when those regimes are underrepresented in training.
Solid and liquid Helmholtz free energies, coexistence temperature, heat of fusion, heat capacity, and phase fractions can be used to benchmark the proposed method.
Deviation greater than approximately 10% from reference ab initio or experimental free energies or fusion properties will falsify the accuracy hypothesis.
